newsitem.title: KENYA: Britain urges Kenya to cool down over elections.
newsitem.headline: Britain urges Kenya to cool down over elections.

text.p: Britain's Africa minister Tony Lloyd said on Friday the Kenyan government had "some way to go" to demonstrate its democratic credentials and urged all politicians to cool down before elections later this year.

"We are calling on the opposition and government politicians to cool the temperature and to make sure the election is conducted in a non-violent atmosphere," said Lloyd, the first minister from Britain's new Labour government to visit Africa.
"We are saying to the government that they have some way to go to demonstrate that the principles a democratic election are held under are actually there," Lloyd told a news conference.
Britain is the largest foreign investor in its former colonial possession and maintains close political and military links.
Lloyd declined to specify how the Kenya African National Union (KANU) government fell short over elections, but said voters and candidates should be free to express their views.

"We are going to play our role in working with the Kenyan people in whatever way we can to make sure that the principles...the democratic rights, the human rights of Kenyan people are respected by all parties," Lloyd said.
President Daniel arap Moi must call presidential and parliamentary elections by the end of 1997.

Opposition parties, church leaders and civic groups under the National Convention Assembly banner have held a series of illegal protests since May to press for a minimum package of constitutional reform before elections.
Opposition leaders say they count on Western diplomats to provide external pressure in their reform campaign.
Lloyd met Moi, opposition and church leaders during his three-nation trip. He came to Kenya after South Africa and continues to Uganda on Saturday.
